title: One brings another (Avot 4:2)
hook: Ben Azzai: run to an easy mitzvah; one good deed draws the next
tomorrow: the person nobody picks: does Ben Azzai have a word?

segments.voice: Yesterday, essentials first: a poor mother's birds before the clever math. Now chapter four opens, with a very strange paycheck.

Apps pay you for a streak with badges, coins and confetti. Ben Azzai offers a stranger reward. Run to an easy mitzvah, he says, and flee from a transgression, for one mitzvah brings another, and one transgression brings another. Then the odd part: the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah. You do a good deed, and your prize is another good deed to do.
screen: `BADGES, COINS, CONFETTI.` → `RUN TO AN EASY ONE.` → `THE PRIZE IS ANOTHER.`

segments.voice: So why pay in the same coin? Start with the run. Ben Azzai doesn't say run to the big, heroic mitzvah. He says the easy one, mitzvah kalah, the one that seems too small to matter. Small things are where habits start, and habits pull. Mitzvah goreret mitzvah: a good deed drags the next one along behind it. Hold one door, and you're already someone who notices the next door. The other direction works the same way, which is why he says flee, not walk. Now the paycheck. Sechar mitzvah, mitzvah. Readers take it more than one way. One: the best reward for doing good is the chance to do more, because the deed is the gift. Another: the deed changes the doer, so the next one comes easier. Either way, the pay isn't outside the deed. It's built in. And since a mitzvah is a commandment, the reward is being asked again.
screen: `RUN TO THE EASY ONE.` · `A DEED DRAGS THE NEXT.` · `FLEE, DON'T WALK.` · `THE PAY IS BUILT IN.` · then, large: `ONE MITZVAH BRINGS ANOTHER.`

segments.voice: Pick the smallest good thing within reach: a dish to put away, a kind reply to a message, water for a plant. Do it now, quickly, while the sit runs. Then notice whether a second small thing shows up on its own.
One brings another. Ben Azzai's mitzvah goreret mitzvah: one good deed pulls the next one behind it.
Keep this one: one mitzvah brings another, and the pay is more of the same. Shalom, friend.
